notice: Unissant confirmed on 2026-10-30 that no charge reference sheet or required-elements checklist will be provided, and supplied a 'Core elements to cover' table as guidance (config/sponsor/unissant-guidance-2026-10-30.json). This checklist (v2) is the team's implementation of that guidance plus the instruction printed on Form I-213: each item names its sponsor category and the case contexts where it applies. The charge summaries are team paraphrases of public statutory text (Title 8 U.S.C.); they are not sponsor-approved and are not legal advice.
historicalNote: Source records date from FY2012-FY2019. Checks compare narratives against the wording recorded here, not against the rules in force on each record's date.

requiredElements.label: Date or time of last entry
requiredElements.description: When the subject last entered or attempted to enter the United States. An approximate date is acceptable.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction: 'time, place and manner of last entry'

requiredElements.label: Place of last entry
requiredElements.description: Where the subject entered. An approximate location such as 'near Brownsville, TX' is acceptable (Unissant clarification). The place of entry is not the same as the place of encounter unless the narrative says so.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction; Unissant email clarification on approximate locations

requiredElements.label: Manner of last entry
requiredElements.description: How the subject entered, for example without inspection on foot, or admitted at a port of entry with a visa.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction: 'time, place and manner of last entry'

requiredElements.label: How the subject was located or apprehended
requiredElements.description: The circumstances of the encounter: when, where, and how the subject was located or apprehended.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction: 'Outline particulars under which alien was located/apprehended'

requiredElements.label: Citizenship or alienage
requiredElements.description: A statement or record establishing the subject's country of citizenship.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction: 'elements which establish administrative and/or criminal violation'

requiredElements.label: Basis for the immigration violation
requiredElements.description: Facts showing the subject lacks lawful status or documents, such as a statement that they have no immigration documents, or that they overstayed an admission.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction: 'elements which establish administrative and/or criminal violation'

requiredElements.label: Means and route of travel to the interior
requiredElements.description: How the subject travelled from the place of entry to where they were found. Advisory: reported in the checklist, not issued as a flag, because the form instruction is general and many valid narratives describe it briefly.
requiredElements.source: Form I-213 narrative block instruction: 'Indicate means and route of travel to interior'

requiredElements.label: Identifying documents
requiredElements.description: Which identity documents the traveler had or presented (passport, ID card, license, visa), or a statement that there were none.
requiredElements.source: Unissant guidance S1 (identity and claimed status)

requiredElements.label: Status or classification claimed for admission
requiredElements.description: The immigration status or classification under which admission was requested.

requiredElements.label: Application for admission: port, documents presented, purpose of travel
requiredElements.description: The port of entry, the documents presented, and the stated purpose of travel.

requiredElements.label: Source of key facts identified
requiredElements.description: Whether important facts say where they came from: the traveler's statement, the officer's observation, or a records check. Advisory: shown in the checklist, not raised as a flag.

requiredElements.label: Specific ground stated and explained
requiredElements.description: The narrative states the precise INA section and subsection and how the facts satisfy it. A bare 'not credible' or 'not a bona fide visitor' is not enough.

requiredElements.label: Traveler's explanation for a discrepancy
requiredElements.description: When the record contains a discrepancy, whether the traveler's explanation or response is recorded and whether it resolves it. Not applicable when no discrepancy is found. Advisory: shown in the checklist, not raised as a separate flag (the discrepancy itself is already a finding routed to a person).

requiredElements.label: Disposition and documenting form
requiredElements.description: What action was taken (for example Notice to Appear, warrant of arrest, reinstatement, expedited removal, voluntary return) and the form documenting it.

requiredElements.label: Expedited removal: advisal, opportunity to respond, review and service
requiredElements.description: In expedited removal: the traveler was advised of the charges and given an opportunity to respond, and required review and service are recorded.

charges.title: Present without admission or parole
charges.plainEnglish: The person is in the United States without having been admitted or paroled, or arrived at a time or place not designated by the government.
keyFacts: Entered without inspection, admission, or parole, or at an undesignated time or place
inconsistentWith: Narrative states the subject was lawfully admitted (for example, on a visa) and the issue is staying past the permitted time

charges.title: Present in violation of law after admission
charges.plainEnglish: The person was admitted but is now in the United States in violation of law, for example by remaining longer than permitted.
keyFacts: Now present in violation of law, such as overstaying
inconsistentWith: Narrative states the subject entered without inspection and was never admitted

charges.title: Immigrant without valid entry document
charges.plainEnglish: At the time of applying for admission, the person did not have a valid visa or other required entry document.
keyFacts: Applied for admission (for example, at a port of entry)
Lacked a valid immigrant visa or entry document at that time
inconsistentWith: Narrative describes entry between ports without any application for admission

charges.title: Improper entry (criminal)
charges.plainEnglish: Entering or attempting to enter at a time or place not designated by immigration officers, eluding inspection, or entering through a false statement.
keyFacts: Entered or attempted entry at an undesignated time or place, eluded inspection, or used a false statement
Facts about when and where the entry happened
inconsistentWith: Narrative states the subject was inspected and admitted at a port of entry

charges.title: Reentry after removal (criminal)
charges.plainEnglish: A person who was previously removed, deported, or denied admission later entered, attempted to enter, or is found in the United States without permission.
keyFacts: Prior removal, deportation, or denial of admission
Later entered, attempted entry, or was found in the United States without consent to reapply
inconsistentWith: Immigration history shows no prior removal

formGlossary.note: Common abbreviations printed in the source forms, as understood by the team. Provisional; used only to help read form fields.
formGlossary.OA / O / PB: Method of location codes; meaning not confirmed, do not interpret

requiresNote: 'requires' is a team-written, machine-checkable summary of each charge's core factual requirement, used for a deterministic citation pre-check. Provisional.

contexts.interior: Interior encounter: located inside the United States (for example by Border Patrol).
contexts.port_of_entry: Application for admission at a port of entry.
contexts.expedited_removal: Processed under expedited removal (may overlap the other contexts).
